question: Using the definition of ADS and Table 5A-1, explain why Level 2 is not an ADS level while Level 3 is.
model_answer: Direct Answer: The MUTCD defines an Automated Driving System (ADS) as hardware and software capable of performing the *entire* Dynamic Driving Task (DDT) on a sustained basis, and states the term applies specifically to Level 3, 4, or 5 systems. In Table 5A-1, a Level 2 system executes only steering and acceleration/deceleration while "the human driver performs all remaining aspects of the Dynamic Driving Task," so it does not perform the entire DDT and is categorized as ADAS. A Level 3 system performs "all aspects of the Dynamic Driving Task within a given ODD" (with a human expected to respond to intervention requests), which meets the ADS definition, so Table 5A-1 groups Levels 3–5 under the "Automated Driving System (ADS)" category. Standards (mandatory): - "The following acronyms and abbreviations, when used in this Manual, shall have the following meanings: … ADS-Automated Driving System …" (This establishes the mandatory meaning of the acronym; the substantive definition itself is Support.) Guidance (recommended): (none) Options (permitted): (none) Support/Definitions (informational): - "Automated Driving System (ADS) – The hardware and software that are collectively capable of performing the entire Dynamic Driving Task (DDT) on a sustained basis, regardless of whether it is limited to a specific Operational Design Domain (ODD); this term is used specifically to describe a Level 3, 4, or 5 driving automation system." - Table 5A-1 describes Level 2 as "the driving mode specific execution by one or more sustained driver assistance systems of both steering and acceleration/deceleration … with the expectation that the human driver performs all remaining aspects of the Dynamic Driving Task," placing it in the "Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS)" category. - Table 5A-1 describes Level 3 as "the driving mode specific sustained performance by an ADS of all aspects of the Dynamic Driving Task within a given ODD with the expectation that the human driver will respond appropriately to a request to intervene," placing it in the "Automated Driving System (ADS)" category. - For background, driving automation system technology "automates some or all aspects of the driving tasks to assist or replace the human driver and can include driver assistance technology generally known as advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS)." Visual evidence: [Image 1] shows Table 5A-1, in which the "Automation Category" column groups Levels 1–2 under "Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS)" and Levels 3–5 under "Automated Driving System (ADS)." [Image 5] shows the full page containing Table 5A-1 together with the Level 2 and Level 3 descriptions confirming that only Levels 3 and above involve an ADS performing all aspects of the DDT. [Image 7] shows the Chapter 5A definitions page, including the ADS definition tying the term specifically to Level 3, 4, or 5 systems. Citations: - Section 5A.03 Support §1 (p.760) - Table 5A-1 (p.760) - Section 1C.03 Standard §1 (p.31) - Section 5A.02 Support §1 (p.759)
gold_answer: An ADS performs the entire dynamic driving task on a sustained basis and the term applies to Levels 3-5. Level 2 performs steering and acceleration/deceleration but still expects the human to perform all remaining aspects of the task, so it is ADAS rather than ADS. Level 3 performs all aspects within its ODD, subject to a human fallback request.
